title: Early clinical and biomarker responses after treatment in patients with non-segmental vitiligo.
projectDescription:
This study was a prospective cohort study in patients with non-segmental vitiligo receiving SoC
treatment. Standard of care treatment involved a potent topical corticosteroid, such as Fluticasone
propionate (FP) cream, used alone or in combination with NB-UVB phototherapy treatment, based on
disease severity per the investigator’s evaluation. For this study, as per institutional guidelines, FP cream
was the first choice for SoC treatment; however, if FP cream was not available, then potent topical
corticosteroids such as Mometasone furoate (i.e. Elocon, Mometason) or betametasone valerate (i.e.
Betnelan, betamethason) were prescribed. Calcineurin inhibitors were used for the face according to the
SoC instead of steroids. Study participation did not affect SoC treatment. The study was conducted at
the Netherlands Institute for Pigment Disorders (NIPD), Department of Dermatology, Amsterdam
University Medical Center (AMC), University of Amsterdam, The Netherlands
dataProcessingProtocol: The proteomics data from blister fluid and blood plasma at baseline and upon treatment was analyzed by SomaLogic technology. Proteomics data was normalized according to the SomaLogic Hyb normalization - median signal normalization procedure. The data was quality controlled and assembled with lab sample data and clinical data to obtain about 4550 log2 transformed human protein quantities per sample.
sampleProcessingProtocol: Skin punch biopsies, of four-millimeter diameter, were collected from the border of a vitiligo lesion at baseline and 3-months after start of therapy (adjacent to the pre-treatment biopsies at the same lesion). These biopsies were dissociated into single cells through enzymatic digestion, by using the Whole Skin Dissociation Kit and mechanical dissociation with the gentleMACSTM Dissociator (both Miltenyi Biotec, Germany). Subsequently, a 70 μm cell strainer was used for filtering and collecting the cells. A suction blister (1 cm diameter) was raised at the border of a lesion and in a non-lesional control area in the same skin region (with similar type of skin) at Baseline. After 3 months of treatment, another suction blister was raised at a predefined area from the original border of the same lesion. From each blister, approximately 400 μL fluid was harvested. The blister fluid was used to study the skin interstitial fluid for its cellular composition or soluble factors before and after therapy in parallel to the skin biopsy analyses.Peripheral blood samples were obtained from all patients at baseline and 3-months. Peripheral Blood. Mononuclear Cells (PBMC) were purified from the peripheral blood by Ficol density gradient centrifugation (Axis-Shield density gradient media, Fresenius Kabi Norge AS, Halden, Norway).
